title: Numerical Patterns, Input-Output Tables and Graphs
seo_title: Grade 5 Numerical Patterns and Input-Output Tables Worksheets (TEKS 5.4C, 5.4D, STAAR)
standard_text: 5.4C generate a numerical pattern when given a rule in the form y = ax or y = x + a and graph; 5.4D recognize the difference between additive and multiplicative numerical patterns given in a table or graph
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 worksheets for Texas TEKS 5.4C and 5.4D: generate patterns from a rule, tell additive and multiplicative patterns apart, use y = ax and y = x + a, graph ordered pairs and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Additive: y = x + a. Multiplicative: y = a × x.
key_sub: Test the rule with every pair in the table.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • An additive pattern adds the same number to x: y = x + 4 gives 1 → 5, 2 → 6, 3 → 7.
  • A multiplicative pattern multiplies x by the same number: y = 4 × x gives 1 → 4, 2 → 8, 3 → 12.
  • Check the rule with every pair in the table, not just one.
  • Each pair (x, y) is a point you can graph on the coordinate plane.

Examples

Example

x: 1, 2, 3, 4 y: 6, 7, 8, 9

7 − 2 = 5 for every pair

Additive

Answer: y = x + 5

Example

x: 1, 2, 3, 4 y: 6, 12, 18, 24

12 ÷ 2 = 6 for every pair

Multiplicative

Answer: y = 6 × x

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Checking only one pairy = x + 5 and y = 6 × x both give 1 → 6. Test the next pair too.
Using the change in y as the ruleIf y goes up by 6, the rule may be y = 6 × x, not y = x + 6.
Switching x and y on the graphx is across, y is up: (2, 12) means 2 right, 12 up.

faq.a: Generate a numerical pattern when given a rule in the form y = ax or y = x + a and graph.
Recognize the difference between additive and multiplicative numerical patterns given in a table or graph.

faq.q: How can I tell additive from multiplicative?
faq.a: Subtract x from y for each pair. If it is always the same, it is additive. If y ÷ x is always the same, it is multiplicative.

faq.q: What does a multiplicative pattern look like on a graph?
faq.a: The points line up on a line that starts at (0, 0).

items.q: Which graph shows the ordered pairs (A term, B term) from the table?
items.e: Graph 3. The pairs are (0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 3), (3, 4): each point is 1 higher than it is far right. Graph 1 has x and y switched.

items.q: Which graph shows the ordered pairs (A term, B term) from the table?
items.e: Graph 2. The pairs are (0, 1), (2, 2), (4, 3). Pattern A goes 0, 2, 4, so the points are 2 apart across. Graph 1 has x and y switched.

items.q: Pattern A: start at 0, Add 1. Pattern B: start at 0, Add 2. Each point is (A term, B term). Which ordered pair does point P show?
items.e: Go down from P to the x-axis: 3. Go across from P to the y-axis: 6. So P is (3, 6), the 4th terms of A and B.

items.q: Pattern A: start at 0, Add 2. Pattern B: start at 0, Add 6. Each point is (A term, B term). Which ordered pair does point P show?
items.e: Go down from P to the x-axis: 4. Go across from P to the y-axis: 12. So P is (4, 12), the 3rd terms of A and B. Read the numbers on the axes, not the number of grid spaces.

items.q: Pattern A: start at 0, Add 1. Pattern B: start at 0, Add 2. The green points show the first 4 ordered pairs. Which red point shows the next ordered pair?
items.e: Point S. Pattern A adds 1 and Pattern B adds 2, so the next pair is (4, 8). (8, 4) has x and y switched, and (4, 7) adds 1 to the B term instead of 2.

items.q: Pattern A: start at 0, Add 2. Pattern B: start at 0, Add 4. The green points show the first 4 ordered pairs. Which red point shows the next ordered pair?
items.e: Point R. Pattern A adds 2 and Pattern B adds 4, so the next pair is (8, 16). (16, 8) has x and y switched, and (10, 20) skips a pair: one jump too many.

items.e: Point P. It is at (2, 1), but the pair is (1, 2): x and y are switched.

items.q: Pattern A: start at 0, Add 2. Pattern B: start at 0, Add 1. Points P, Q, R and S should show the 2nd to 5th ordered pairs (A term, B term). Which point was plotted wrong?
items.e: Point R. It is at (6, 4), but the 4th A term, 6, goes with the 4th B term, 3. The point uses the next B term.

items.q: Pattern A: start at 1, Add 1. Pattern B: start at 3, Add 1. Points P, Q, R and S should show the 2nd to 5th ordered pairs (A term, B term). Which point was plotted wrong?
items.e: Point P. It is at (2, 5), but the 2nd A term, 2, goes with the 2nd B term, 4. The point uses the next B term.

items.q: Pattern A: start at 0, Add 3. Pattern B: start at 0, Add 9. The ordered pairs (A term, B term) are graphed. Which point is also on the graph?
items.e: Each B term is 3 times the A term, so 15 goes with 45: (15, 45). (15, 24) adds 9 and (15, 18) adds 3 instead of using the relationship.

items.q: Pattern A: start at 0, Add 2. Pattern B: start at 0, Add 6. The point (6, 18) is on the graph. How do you get from it to the next point?
items.e: The x-coordinate is the A term, which grows by 2. The y-coordinate is the B term, which grows by 6. So move right 2 and up 6, to (8, 24).

items.q: On a graph of (A term, B term), every point has a y-coordinate that is 4 times its x-coordinate. What does this tell you?
c: Each B term is 4 times the A term
Each A term is 4 times the B term
Each B term is 4 more than the A term
items.e: The x-coordinate is the A term and the y-coordinate is the B term. y = 4 × x means each B term is 4 times the corresponding A term.

items.q: Pattern A: start at 0, Add 2. Pattern B: start at 0, Add 4. What do you notice about the graphed points?
c: They are all on the x-axis
They go down to the right
They are on a straight line
items.e: Each step goes right 2 and up 4, the same move every time, so the points line up in a straight line that starts at the origin.

items.q: Pattern A: start at 0, Add 5. Pattern B: start at 0, Add 15. The first graphed point is (0, 0). What does it show?
c: It is not a pair of terms
items.e: (0, 0) is the 1st ordered pair: the 1st term of A is 0 and the 1st term of B is 0.

items.q: Luis is 6 years older than his cousin. Which rule gives Luis's age y when the cousin is x years old? How old is Luis when the cousin is 13?
items.e: The difference in age never changes, so add 6: y = x + 6. 13 + 6 = 19.

items.q: Diego has $43 more than his brother. Which rule gives Diego's money y if his brother has x dollars? How much does Diego have if his brother has $33?
items.e: Diego always has $43 more, so add: y = x + 43. 33 + 43 = $76.
